solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Poet program occupies most of exhibit (6)

indicatorNotes.occupies: the program takes up room inside the exhibit

blocks.note: SHOW = exhibit, minus its final W
an app is a computer program

annotation.surface: A poet's software sits in a gallery display, taking up nearly all of it.
annotation.walkthrough: Program is the modern software sense, an unexpected neighbour for a poet from the sixth century BC.
annotation.definitionFit: Sappho is one of the most famous poets of ancient Greece.

entries.clue: Buffeted small railway wagon (6)

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
in Britain an open railway goods wagon is a truck

annotation.surface: A little railway wagon is knocked about by the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: Buffeted reads as an adjective describing the wagon, but it is the past tense of a verb: hit, struck.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: waves or wind that buffet a thing hit it hard.

entries.clue: Legal cases succeeded against local press agent (9)

indicatorNotes.cases: LICIT encloses S, like a case round its contents
indicatorNotes.against: PUB is placed up against the rest

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub

annotation.surface: Lawsuits are won against a regional newspaper's PR person.
annotation.walkthrough: Legal cases looks like a noun phrase about lawsuits; it is LICIT casing S. 'Local' as a noun is British for the neighbourhood pub.
annotation.definitionFit: A publicist handles press and publicity for a client.

entries.clue: It’s perfect on top of yoghurt! (5)

annotation.definition: It’s perfect on top of yoghurt!

indicatorNotes.on top of: take the top, first letter of yoghurt

blocks.note: to hone is to perfect, as a skill

annotation.surface: A cheerful food writer's verdict: nothing beats a drizzle over yoghurt.
annotation.walkthrough: Perfect looks like an adjective but is the verb HONE. The whole sentence is also the definition: honey is the perfect topping for yoghurt.
annotation.definitionFit: Honey drizzled over yoghurt is a classic pairing.

entries.clue: Dish made with eggs — some sell better without any shells (8)

indicatorNotes.without any shells: each word loses its outer letters, as an egg loses its shell

blocks.note: sOMe without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A market trader's tip: eggs sell better once you have taken the shells off.
annotation.walkthrough: The shells are the first and last letters of each of the three words; the egg imagery makes the instruction apt.
annotation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked in a pan.

entries.clue: Doctor claimed refurbished workspace next to river (7,7)

indicatorNotes.refurbished: CLAIMED is done up into a new form

annotation.surface: A doctor says a renovated office by the river is theirs.
annotation.walkthrough: Doctor reads as a title in the surface; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical officer is a doctor in charge of health in an organisation or area.

entries.clue: Call in large loan agreements, causing reputational damage (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the call sits within the loan agreements

blocks.note: l = large, as on clothing labels
IOUs are written promises to repay
to bell someone is British slang for phoning them

annotation.surface: A bank calls in big loans, and its good name suffers for it.
annotation.walkthrough: Call in reads as the banking phrase for demanding repayment; here Call is BELL and in tells you where it goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Something libellous damages a person's reputation in writing.

entries.clue: Every now and again swim past rocky peak in trunks (5)

indicatorNotes.Every now and again: take every other letter of swim
indicatorNotes.past: to swim past something is to go beyond it, so the swim letters come after the peak

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
S, I: letters 1 and 3 of swim

annotation.surface: A swimmer in trunks occasionally paddles past a craggy outcrop.
annotation.walkthrough: Trunks are swimwear in the surface but are bodies without limbs in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Torsi is a plural of torso, the trunk of the body.

entries.clue: Invigorate Frenchman upset with non-uniform appearance (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, turn RENE upside down
indicatorNotes.non-uniform: remove U, which is uniform in the phonetic alphabet

blocks.note: RENE, a French man's name, turned over
GUISE = appearance, with its U taken away

annotation.surface: Pep up a troubled French chap who looks scruffy and out of uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: Non-uniform suggests irregular; it means take out U.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to fill someone with energy and vigour.

entries.clue: Note lines accompanying lengthy word for part of the brain (4-4,6)

annotation.definitionNote: strictly a function of the brain rather than a physical part of it

indicatorNotes.accompanying: MEMO and RY go along with LONG TERM

blocks.note: RY = railway, whose lines are its tracks

annotation.surface: A long technical word noted down as a label for a brain region.
annotation.walkthrough: Lines for RY is a standard crossword shorthand: railway lines.
annotation.definitionFit: Long-term memory is the brain's store of lasting memories.

entries.clue: Heroic tale of Ohio-born Liberal Democrat (5,4)

annotation.definitionNote: Robin Hood is the hero of the tale, and his name is used for the tale itself

indicatorNotes.Liberal: take liberties with the letters of OHIO-BORN

blocks.note: d = Democrat, as in US politics

annotation.surface: A political tale about a hero born in Ohio who stood for the Liberal Democrats.
annotation.walkthrough: Liberal Democrat is a UK party name, but Liberal is the anagram signal and only Democrat gives a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the English outlaw hero of the ballads and tales told about him.

entries.clue: Seize westbound drug boat (5)

indicatorNotes.westbound: an across answer reads west to east, so going west runs GRAB right to left

annotation.surface: Customs officers board a smuggling boat heading west with narcotics.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drug bust at sea; in fact the boat is the definition and seize is the word that turns.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a barge is a flat-bottomed cargo vessel used on canals and rivers.

entries.clue: Life force found within Pinocchio (3)

indicatorNotes.found within: the answer sits inside the name

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of the puppet's name, after PINO

annotation.surface: The spark that makes a wooden puppet come alive.
annotation.walkthrough: Pinocchio is the puppet who came to life, so the life force fits the story too.
annotation.definitionFit: Chi (qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy.

entries.clue: Compare story-telling with cartoon bear leading and jumping cross-legged (5,6)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means together with, so the compare and story-telling pieces are joined side by side
indicatorNotes.leading: whoever is leading walks in front, so the bear goes at the start of the answer

blocks.note: Yogi Bear of the Hanna-Barbera cartoons
cf. is the abbreviation for compare

annotation.surface: A children's storyteller compares tales with a cartoon bear who hops about in a lotus pose.
annotation.walkthrough: Story-telling is the childish euphemism for fibbing. Yogic flying is the Transcendental Meditation practice of hopping while seated cross-legged.
annotation.definitionFit: Yogic flying is hopping along while sitting in the lotus position.

entries.clue: Combine core part of chimney and old fireplace (6)

indicatorNotes.core part of: the core of anything is its centre, so take the letter at the very middle of the word

blocks.note: M is the central letter of chiMney
an ingle is an old word for a hearth, as in inglenook

annotation.surface: Building instructions: join the middle of the chimney stack to an antique hearth.
annotation.walkthrough: Combine is a verb here, matching mingle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to mix things together.

entries.clue: Laid songs out in series of notes (9)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are laid out in a new order

annotation.surface: A composer sets out their songs as a run of musical notes.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface keeps you thinking of scores; the answer is itself a musical term, a slide through a run of notes.
annotation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide up or down through a series of notes.

entries.clue: Hunter — one regularly taking fewer traps (7)

indicatorNotes.traps: LESS holds I and ON inside it

blocks.note: on a medicine is regularly taking it

annotation.surface: A hunter who sets fewer traps than before.
annotation.walkthrough: Regularly taking looks like an alternate-letters instruction, but it means ON, as in on statins. It is the lioness, not the lion, who does most of a pride's hunting.
annotation.definitionFit: Lionesses do most of the hunting for a pride.

entries.clue: Something that reveals palpebral muscle? (3-6)

blocks.note: a surprising discovery that shows you something you had not seen
palpebral means of the eyelid; the muscle literally opens the eye

annotation.surface: An anatomy question about what shows the eyelid muscle.
annotation.walkthrough: Palpebral is an obscure word for 'of the eyelid'; the muscle that lifts the lid is literally an eye opener.
annotation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, and a muscle that raises the eyelid opens the eye.

entries.clue: Lift across the pond to reveal rocks (8)

indicatorNotes.rocks: the letters are rocked into a new order

annotation.surface: An American lift opens to show a pile of stones.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocks is a noun in the surface but a verb here. Across the pond means in America.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: what Britons call a lift, Americans (across the Atlantic) call by this name.

entries.clue: Set fire to gas when there’s no energy left for element (7)

blocks.clueFragment: gas when there’s no energy left
blocks.note: HELIUM, a gas, without E and L

annotation.surface: A chemist ignites a gas once its energy has run out, to obtain an element.
annotation.walkthrough: No energy left sounds like exhaustion; it removes two letters, E for energy and L for left.
annotation.definitionFit: Lithium is a chemical element, the lightest metal.

entries.clue: Someone going through penance more quickly (6)

blocks.note: one who fasts, as in Lent

annotation.surface: A penitent hurrying through their penance.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced the same but come from different roots: going without food, and speed.
annotation.definitionFit: A faster abstains from food as penance; faster also means more quickly.

entries.clue: Pretence regularly cloaked by quiet delivery (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take letters at a steady every-other spacing

annotation.surface: A soft-spoken way of talking that masks a pretence.
annotation.walkthrough: Delivery means a way of speaking here, not a parcel arriving.
annotation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is their speech, the way they talk.

entries.clue: Five nudes jumping over tree backwards — it’s a work of art (5,2,4)

indicatorNotes.jumping: the letters of NUDES leap about
indicatorNotes.backwards: O and LIME are read in reverse

annotation.surface: Five naked figures leap backwards over a tree, which sounds like a sculpture.
annotation.walkthrough: O and LIME make OLIME, which reverses to EMILO. The nudes fit the famous armless statue.
annotation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is the ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

entries.clue: Group performing without safety device? (5)

indicatorNotes.without: in its old sense of outside: NET goes around ON

annotation.surface: Trapeze artists perform without a safety net.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface splits the answer as 'no net', which is exactly the trap: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, as in the hymn line 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is a group of nine performers, or a piece written for them.

entries.clue: Bad egg turning green (5)

indicatorNotes.turning: EVIL and O are turned round together

annotation.surface: A rotten egg going green.
annotation.walkthrough: Bad egg is a set phrase for a rogue, which hides the split between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish-green colour.

entries.clue: Love intervening for and on behalf of father (3)

indicatorNotes.intervening: O comes between the two P's

blocks.note: pp = per procurationem, written when signing for someone else

annotation.surface: Love steps in to speak up for Dad.
annotation.walkthrough: pp is what you write before signing a letter on someone else's behalf.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, chiefly American word for a dad.

entries.clue: Muscle connector lacks density for part of joint (5)

indicatorNotes.lacks: a thing that lacks something does not have it, so the letter for density is removed

blocks.note: a tendon joins muscle to bone

annotation.surface: An anatomy note: a tendon missing its density, in part of a knee.
annotation.walkthrough: The anatomy surface makes you think of a body joint; the answer is a carpentry joint.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into a mortise to make a joint.

entries.clue: Honour the German church incorporating new submissiveness (9)

indicatorNotes.incorporating: to incorporate is to take into the body of something, so 'the German church' takes the new letter into itself

blocks.note: OBE = Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

annotation.surface: Honouring a German church that has brought in a new meekness.
annotation.walkthrough: The German looks like a nationality; it asks for the German word for 'the'. DIE and CE together take N in at their join.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a willingness to do as one is told.

entries.clue: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology? (8)

annotation.definition: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology?

indicatorNotes.Revised: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters of name or term are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.accommodating: to accommodate a guest is to give them room, so the reworked letters make room for one more
indicatorNotes.latest in: the latest in a sequence is the one at the end, so take the final letter

annotation.surface: A dictionary definition of a new name forced on an old thing by modern tech.
annotation.walkthrough: N for name is a dictionary abbreviation. The whole clue is also the definition: a retronym renames something because technology moved on, as with 'acoustic guitar'.
annotation.definitionFit: A retronym is a new name for an old thing, coined after a newer version appeared.

entries.clue: Go through curved opening at 135 degrees (6)

blocks.note: on a compass, 135 degrees is south-east
an arch is a curved opening

annotation.surface: Walk through a rounded doorway set at an angle.
annotation.walkthrough: 135 degrees looks like geometry; it is a compass bearing, south-east.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going through someone's pockets means hunting through them.
